content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken grilled and coated with sauce is a popular dish in many cuisines worldwide. The meat is high in protein, and the lack of skin reduces fat content, making it a lighter option.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken is one of the most consumed meats globally.
Grilling creates a distinctive flavor through the Maillard reaction.
Various sauces (barbecue, teriyaki, garlic) dramatically change the taste profile.
Chicken provides all essential amino acids.
In some cultures, skinless chicken is considered a healthier choice.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving delivers about 31 g of high‑quality protein, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Removing the skin cuts saturated fat, which is beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken contains niacin (B3), vitamin B6, and B12, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It provides phosphorus, selenium, and zinc, important for bones, immunity, and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Chicken protein is quickly absorbed, making it suitable for athletes and recovery periods.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Sauces often contain high salt levels; choose low‑sodium versions if you have hypertension.

items.title: Additives
items.content: Some ready‑made sauces may contain artificial preservatives and sweeteners.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Skinless grilled chicken can be served as a main dish, sliced into salads, used in sandwiches, or added to pasta. Sauces can be served on the side or drizzled over the meat just before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked chicken in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions at –18 °C; thaw in the refrigerator before reheating.
